Payroll Processing Procedures

Purpose
These procedures define how the company prepares, validates, approves, and communicates each payroll cycle. Consistent payroll operations are essential for employee trust, legal compliance, and financial control. Payroll is processed semi-monthly unless a local business unit follows a legally required alternative schedule approved by Finance and HR.

Source Data and Ownership
Payroll relies on source data from the HRIS, timekeeping platform, approved compensation change records, leave management records, and benefit deduction files. HR Operations owns employee master data accuracy. Managers own timely approval of hours, overtime, and attendance exceptions. Finance reviews payroll funding and unusual cost movement. Payroll Specialists own final calculation review and submission to the payroll provider.

Payroll Calendar
At the start of each quarter, Payroll publishes cutoff dates for time approval, adjustment submissions, and pay dates. Managers must approve all prior-period hours by 12:00 p.m. local time on the published cutoff day. Changes submitted after the cutoff are processed in the next payroll cycle unless Payroll approves an urgent off-cycle correction. The official payroll calendar is stored in the shared HR workspace and communicated to all people managers.

Processing Steps
Step one: load approved hours, leave codes, earnings, and deduction changes from source systems. Step two: reconcile new hires, terminations, compensation changes, and bank updates against HRIS records. Step three: run preliminary payroll calculations and produce an exception report showing missing approvals, negative net pay, unusual overtime, duplicate earnings, and inactive employees with payable balances. Step four: investigate and correct exceptions with HR, managers, or Finance. Step five: generate the final preview register and obtain dual approval from Payroll and Finance. Step six: submit the approved file to the payroll provider and confirm successful acceptance. Step seven: issue employee communication if there are holidays, deadline shifts, or known processing notes.

Off-Cycle Payments
Off-cycle payroll may be used for material underpayments, termination final pay obligations, or approved bonus corrections. Requests must include root cause, amount, employee impact, and approving leader. Payroll evaluates tax and deduction handling before release. Convenience requests or last-minute manager errors do not automatically qualify for off-cycle payment.

Controls and Audit Requirements
No single person may create, approve, and release the same payroll adjustment. Access to bank data, compensation updates, and payroll registers is restricted by role. Payroll retains registers, approval evidence, and adjustment support for the retention period required by law and company policy. Any discrepancy affecting more than three employees or more than $2,500 in aggregate must be logged as a payroll incident and reviewed post-payroll for corrective action.

Employee Support
Employees should report pay issues within five business days of receiving pay. Payroll acknowledges all tickets within one business day and provides either a resolution timeline or a request for more information. Sensitive payroll data should never be sent over unsecured channels.

Escalation
Potential wage-and-hour compliance issues, repeated deduction errors, or unauthorized compensation changes must be escalated immediately to the Head of HR Operations and Finance Controller.

Post-Payroll Review
After each payroll closes, Payroll and HR Operations perform a brief retrospective covering exception trends, root causes, off-cycle volume, and missed cutoffs. Action items from the review are documented with owners and due dates so recurring issues can be reduced in future cycles.
